questions.question: What is the name of the Roman general played by Russell Crowe in Gladiator (2000), the role that won him the Academy Award for Best Actor?
questions.note: Crowe's Maximus earned him the Best Actor Oscar — the third of three consecutive nominations.

questions.question: Which range of hills, running from Derbyshire up to Northumberland, is often called 'the backbone of England'?
questions.note: The range earns the nickname from its length and its position straight down the middle of northern England.

questions.question: In which year was the Royal Academy of Arts founded in London, with Joshua Reynolds as its first president?
questions.note: Reynolds, the leading portrait painter of his day, was the obvious choice to lead the new Academy.

questions.question: In 1620 the Mayflower made its final departure from England from which port on the Devon coast?
questions.note: After the leaky Speedwell was abandoned, the Mayflower sailed alone on 16 September 1620 and reached Cape Cod 66 days later.

questions.question: Traditionally, was the Yorkshire pudding served with gravy before the meat course, or after it?
questions.note: Cheap batter pudding was served first with gravy to fill people up, so the expensive roast would stretch further.

questions.question: Which chemical element takes its name from a small Scottish village where its mineral was first discovered?
questions.note: The village of Strontian on Loch Sunart gave its name to the mineral strontianite, and then to the element isolated by Humphry Davy in 1808.

questions.question: Which island, separated from Hampshire by the Solent, is the largest island of England?
questions.note: At about 380 km² it is comfortably England's largest island, well ahead of Sheppey and Hayling.

questions.question: William Hogarth's original set of eight paintings 'A Rake's Progress', one of which is shown here, hangs in which London museum?
questions.imageAlt: A crowded, riotous 18th-century tavern scene painted in rich detail
questions.imageCredit: A Rake's Progress III: The Tavern Scene, William Hogarth · Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
questions.note: The architect John Soane bought the eight canvases at auction in 1802, and they still hang in his Lincoln's Inn Fields house.

questions.question: Which cricket club, founded in 1787 and still the custodian of the Laws of Cricket, has its home at Lord's in St John's Wood?
questions.note: The MCC took charge of the Laws the year after its founding, and Lord's is nicknamed the Home of Cricket.

questions.question: In A Beautiful Mind (2001), Russell Crowe plays the real-life John Nash. What was Nash's profession?
questions.note: Nash was a Nobel Prize-winning mathematician famed for his work on game theory, and the film won four Oscars including Best Picture.

questions.question: English borrowed 'etiquette' from French in the 18th century, but the original Old French word meant something much more everyday. What did it mean?
questions.note: The same Old French root also gave English the word 'ticket'; the polite-behaviour sense is thought to come from little cards of court instructions.

questions.question: The Jurassic Coast, England's only natural World Heritage Site, runs along Dorset and East Devon. How many miles long is it?
questions.note: UNESCO describes it as a 95-mile site, inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2001 for its 185 million years of rock.

questions.question: Three of these painters belonged to the same movement. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: The other three were Fauves — the 'wild beasts' named by critic Louis Vauxcelles at the 1905 Salon d'Automne. Degas was an Impressionist.

questions.question: In which year did Florence Nightingale and her nurses arrive at the British military hospital at Scutari during the Crimean War?
questions.note: They left London on 21 October 1854 — a war in which Britain and France fought side by side against Russia.

questions.question: Which famous London department store claims to have invented the Scotch egg in 1738?
questions.note: Fortnum's says it created them for wealthy travellers setting out by carriage from its Piccadilly shop — though rival origin stories exist.

questions.question: Which of these metals is the odd one out?
questions.note: Gold, iron and copper are all solid at room temperature. Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at normal temperatures.

questions.question: In which year was Gladiator, with Russell Crowe as Maximus, released?
questions.note: Gladiator was released in 2000 and won five Academy Awards, including Best Picture.

questions.question: Which cape on France's Côte d'Opale is the closest point of France to Great Britain?
questions.note: Its cliffs are only about 34 km from England — close enough to see the Dover cliffs on a clear day.

questions.question: On the course used for the Oxford v Cambridge Boat Race, which end is the starting line: Putney or Mortlake?
questions.note: Crews start just downstream of Putney Bridge and finish at Mortlake, over 4 miles 374 yards of the Thames.

questions.question: In which city did the young Vincent van Gogh live and work for the art dealers Goupil & Cie from 1873, long before he moved to France?
questions.note: He lodged at 87 Hackford Road in Stockwell while working at Goupil's London branch, and his drawing of that house is his first known work.
